findings.title: Dead/wasted ASN1Encoder calls before building actual sequence
findings.body: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, two throwaway ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls are made (lines 114-115) whose results are discarded entirely before building the real DER sequence a few lines later. This is dead code that does nothing useful, wastes allocations, and is confusing/misleading to maintainers reading the encoding logic — it looks like a leftover from development that should be removed.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider misuses KeyStore provider as 'the' BC provider
findings.body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider backing KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(). This is fragile: the default keystore type's provider is not necessarily BouncyCastle (it could be SUN, PKCS11, etc. depending on JVM/platform configuration), yet CryptoProvider callers elsewhere in the codebase assume this method returns a BC-compatible provider. This can silently return the wrong provider on some platforms, causing unexpected failures or incorrect security provider usage downstream.

findings.title: Silent provider selection replaces previous fail-fast behavior on multiple providers
findings.body: Previously, detecting multiple CryptoProvider implementations on the classpath threw IllegalStateException to force explicit configuration. Now it silently picks the provider with the highest order() and only logs at debug level which providers were ignored. In production deployments where debug logging is disabled, this means a misconfigured classpath with multiple incompatible crypto providers (e.g., accidentally bundling authz-client with the main server) will silently select one without any visible warning, which can hide subtle and hard-to-diagnose cryptographic configuration errors.

findings.title: New abstract method order() breaks binary/source compatibility for third-party CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: Adding a new non-default abstract method order() to the CryptoProvider interface is a breaking change for any third-party or external implementations of this interface (e.g. keycloak-client repo or other consumers) that are not updated to implement it. Since this is a public SPI interface loaded via ServiceLoader, this will cause compile and runtime failures for existing implementations until they add the method. Consider providing a default implementation to preserve backward compatibility.
